content.thinking:
Since the caller isn't authorised, I shouldn't disclose any details—I can offer to pass a message, suggest a consent route, or mention a third-party payment option with just the property address, no balance. I'll let the tenant know via email who called and ask for their consent, being mindful this tenant seems vulnerable and "very down," which raises a wellbeing concern worth handling gently, perhaps flagging support resources without disclosing arrears details.

There's no caller number to log a message to, so I'll proceed with logging the call and sending the tenant an email, while deciding the wellbeing concern is secondhand and modest enough to skip formal escalation but still worth a supportive note. I also notice the caller's DOB claim matches the record, though DOB alone isn't sufficient to confirm authority, and the account shows no guarantor on file.

arguments.party_name: Grace (caller, says she is Jonah Okafor's mother and guarantor)
arguments.summary: Caller asked for rent balance, payment history since summer and tenant's new mobile; wants to pay arrears. Record shows no guarantor, no authorised contacts, no consent to share. Disclosed nothing (no balance, payments, contact details, and did not confirm anything from the record). Explained: we can pass a message to Jonah; Jonah can give written consent or add her as an authorised contact; she can pay towards rent as a third party by quoting the property address (27 Bethnal Green Road) without being told the balance. Knowing address and date of birth is not authority.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who said she is your mum, Grace, rang us today. She said she is worried about you and would like to help with your rent. We did not share any information about your account or your contact details with her. We told her we can pass on a message, that you can give us written consent or add her as an authorised contact, and that she can pay towards the rent by quoting the property address. Please reply to let us know whether you are happy for us to speak to her or share anything, and whether you would like us to pass a message on. If you'd like to talk to someone, Samaritans are on 116 123 any time. We'll look out for your reply and follow up by email on Wednesday 14 October if we haven't heard.

arguments.purpose: Check tenant's reply on consent for Grace (caller claiming to be mother/guarantor); no guarantor or authorised contact on record.

I'll let the tenant know via email who called and ask for their consent, being mindful this tenant seems vulnerable and "very down," which raises a wellbeing concern worth handling gently, perhaps flagging support resources without disclosing arrears details.

There's no caller number to log a message to, so I'll proceed with logging the call and sending the tenant an email, while deciding the wellbeing concern is secondhand and modest enough to skip formal escalation but still worth a supportive note. arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who said she is your mum, Grace, rang us today. She said she is worried about you and would like to help with your rent. We did not share any information about your account or your contact details with her. We told her we can pass on a message, that you can give us written consent or add her as an authorised contact, and that she can pay towards the rent by quoting the property address. Please reply to let us know whether you are happy for us to speak to her or share anything, and whether you would like us to pass a message on. If you'd like to talk to someone, Samaritans are on 116 123 any time. We'll look out for your reply and follow up by email on Wednesday 14 October if we haven't heard.
